_note: What a creature leaves behind, by canonical name and in per-mille. The order matters: it is the order the stream is drawn in, so a seeded walk replays only while it holds. The rates are not the same because the pit does not deal its three creatures the same: `draw_enemy` weights a pool so its hardest member is its rarest, and in The End of All Gears that is eighty encounters in ninety-seven for an A. Rat, sixteen for a toad and ONE for a Wallspider Swarm. So the rate has to carry what the draw does not, and `a_set_is_a_few_hours_and_not_a_lifetime` measures what a player actually counts — wins in the region that holds the creature, drawn with the real weighting. Even at the ceiling the Wallspider Weave is the far end of the band; the pool weight is what would fix that properly and that is the human's call. See PLAN.md 6a. **M11.5's three are the instruments' supporters**, and they are here rather than on a shelf for the reason a quest reward is: what an instrument is worth is the walk that assembled it. All three live in the Stack's Shadow, which is the band you cross to reach the tower the shards come off — so the grind for the parts and the grind for the cores are the same walk. **M11.9's five farmable sets.** One per gated region of West Bambulon, lowest first, so each crossing has a set worth farming behind it \u2014 `PLAN-M11.md` §8 row 7 — plus one on the Treyway. Every one is off the creature its region draws *most*, which is §6b row 1 obeyed rather than paid off: a set behind the rarest fight is a set nobody finishes, and this block has now found that three times. The sixth set is the tower's and is not here: its three pieces are certainties off three floor bosses, so climbing is the grind.
